title: Tuning the Atomic Number Sensitivity in Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Atomic number (Z) sensitivity has long been a major benefit of high-angle annular dark field (HAADF) imaging, making it a popular electron microscopy imaging technique for material analysis. HAADF imaging has Z-contrast following a Zm dependence, with previous literature reporting m in the range of 1.7 – 2.0 [1-3]. This Zm dependence does not, however, usually provide sufficient contrast to distinguish between elements that are very close in atomic number, nor is it usually able to resolve low-Z elements such as oxygen or nitrogen. In contrast, phase-contrast imaging techniques can resolve low-Z elements but are often limited in their atomic number sensitivity/interpretability due to lens aberrations and dynamical scattering depending on the sample thickness [4]. The recent development of multislice electron ptychography overcomes these challenges and enables deep sub-angstrom spatial resolution [5]. Although several studies report an approximately Z1 (linear) [6] or a Z0.67 dependence [5], a comprehensive investigation of this Z-dependence over a broader range of atomic numbers is needed.
